intro: Paste the decision — what you would cut, the sentiment cost as a number with its duration and who would have to agree, what it funds, and what you protect — plus the 300–400 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited; the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, CPO / CHRO track — for sitting Chief People Officers and CHROs. Module 4 applied activity, 'The first cut': a three-part decision about the learner's OWN function. (1) What they would cut — the first process or role they would automate or consolidate, named specifically with roughly how much capacity it consumes and who currently does it; if they cannot name one, that is a finding about their operating-system tier and the write-up should say what it means. (2) The sentiment cost they will absorb — a number on their own metric plus a duration, and then the harder half: who would have to agree to that number and whether it has ever been discussed with them, since a tolerance that has not been socialized is not a tolerance. (3) What it funds — named and specific; if the honest answer is that the saving gets banked, that is legitimate in some conditions PROVIDED the write-up then addresses why the function should continue to be led by a CPO rather than run down. (4) What they protect even under pressure, and why it compounds — IBM's was the entry point. SCORING NOTES. Credit a socialized tolerance far above an asserted one; the module's whole argument is that transformations die at month four when the number was never agreed with the person who asks. Credit a learner who admits they would not actually do this — the write-up asks directly whether they have written a plan they have no intention of starting, and that admission is more useful than a confident plan that will not survive. Where the learner cannot name a cut at all, score at full credit if they account for what that implies. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is the sequencing rule: no standing to tell another function to redesign until you have done it to your own. Its real counter-argument is that this is a moral intuition dressed as a strategic one — nobody asks the CFO to automate finance before advising on capital allocation — and the sharper version, that going first means a People function in the trough of its own transformation cannot support a restructure elsewhere, with the cost borne by employees who had no part in the sequencing decision. Strong positions say what they would do if a major restructure landed on their function in month four. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade the accuracy of the predicted dip, grade the account of the gap — and note specifically whether the learner's number moved after meeting the case, and what it had been anchored on before.

**"Our evidence cannot settle this" scores at full credit where it is the honest answer.** A submission that states plainly what its evidence cannot establish, and why, has done the exercise correctly — never mark it down for declining to reach a conclusion its evidence does not support. Reaching a confident conclusion on thin evidence is the error; naming the limit is the skill.

opening.label: Predicted — the low point service satisfaction would reach before recovering
opening.hint: On a −100 to +100 scale, or state your own scale and give the number in it.

calibration.label: Revised — the tolerance you would actually set now
calibration.hint: Most people revise this deeper after meeting the case. What was the first number anchored on?

dimensions.name: The cut is named and sized
dimensions.criteria: A specific process or role in the learner's own function, with roughly how much capacity it consumes and who currently does it — not a category like 'transactional work' or 'tier-one queries'. Credit a cut that would be genuinely uncomfortable over a safe one. Where the learner cannot name a cut, score at full credit provided they account for what that implies about their operating-system tier.

dimensions.name: The tolerance is a number, and it has been socialized
dimensions.criteria: The discriminating dimension. A number and a duration on the learner's own metric is the minimum. The graded part is who would have to agree and whether it has been discussed — a tolerance that exists only in the learner's head is the failure mode the module describes, since month four is when it gets tested by someone who never agreed to it. Credit an honest 'no, and here is when I will have that conversation' above a confident number with no owner.

dimensions.name: What it funds is named and compounds
dimensions.criteria: A specific destination for the freed capacity, preferably capability that compounds rather than a one-off. 'More strategic work' fails this dimension. Banking the saving is acceptable and must then be paired with an answer to why the function should continue to be led by a CPO — a learner who banks the saving and addresses that honestly scores well; one who banks it without noticing the implication does not.

dimensions.name: What is protected, and why
dimensions.criteria: One thing the learner will not touch under pressure, with a reason that explains why it compounds. IBM's was the entry point, on the reasoning that automating junior work while cutting junior hiring dries the well in three to five years. Credit a protection whose logic is about future capability rather than present sentiment.

dimensions.name: The position engages the sequencing objection
dimensions.criteria: A committed position on the sequencing rule that meets its real counter-argument — that executives advise on things they have not done, constantly, and that going first can leave the function unable to support a restructure elsewhere at the moment it is most needed. Required element: what they would do if a major restructure landed on their function in month four. A position that endorses the rule without addressing that scenario has not tested it.

dimensions.name: The delta, and whether they would actually do it
dimensions.criteria: The predicted dip against the revised tolerance, with an account of what moved — and specifically what the first number had been anchored on, which is usually nothing. Accuracy is never graded. Plus the module's closing question: whether they would actually do this or have written a plan they have no intention of starting. Credit that admission highly; it is the honest answer for many people in this seat, and a submission that reaches it has understood the module better than one that performs resolve.
